summary: This standards-track document adds an entry to the registry of properties used in Authentication-Results mail header fields. It lets a mail system pass along the result of a Vouch By Reference query, a method for a trusted party to vouch for the sender. Later mail systems can then see that result.

eli5.summary: When mail arrives, the receiver can write notes about checks made. This adds a place to note whether someone trustworthy vouched for the sender.

questions: how to record vbr result in email header
subtitle: A small registry update that lets a mail system record the outcome of a Vouch By Reference check in a message header.

tldr.problem: A border mail gateway can ask a vouching service whether a trusted third party stands behind a sender's domain, but there was no standard way to pass that answer on to filters and mail clients inside the network.
tldr.mechanism: The memo registers a new method, vbr, with two properties, header.md and header.mv, and five result codes for use in the Authentication-Results header field.
tldr.outcome: A VBR result can now be relayed as an annotation in a message header. What a receiver does with it is left to local policy.

facts.label: Registry updated
facts.value: Email Authentication Methods and Result Names

today: RFC 6212 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 5451 and RFC 5518.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 5451 defined the Authentication-Results header field, which presents the results of a message authentication effort in a machine-readable format. Meanwhile, a proposal for rudimentary domain-level reputation assessment called Vouch By Reference (VBR) had been published as RFC 5518 and was, in the words of this memo, beginning to see popular use.

RFC 6212 is deliberately small. It registers one more reporting property so that a VBR result can be relayed as an annotation in a message header.
sections.eli5: There was already a place on a message to write down what checks it passed. This memo adds one more kind of check to that list.

sections.title: Vouch By Reference and Why Relay It
sections.content:
Vouch By Reference lets a message receiver query a "vouching" service to find out whether a trusted third party is willing to state that mail from a particular source can be considered legitimate.

When that assessment is done at an inbound border mail gateway, it is useful to relay the result to internal mail entities such as filters or user agents. The Authentication-Results field already exists for this kind of reporting, so the memo reuses it rather than inventing a new field.

The memo does not say how to react to a result. Reactions to an Authentication-Results field containing VBR (or any) results are entirely a matter of local policy at the receiver.
sections.eli5: A guard at the front door asks a trusted friend, "is this visitor okay?" and then wants to tell the people inside the house what the friend said. How the people inside act on it is up to them.

sections.title: The vbr Method and Its Properties
sections.content:
The memo adds the method vbr to the "Email Authentication Methods" registry that IANA created when RFC 5451 was published. Two properties (reporting items) go with it: header.md and header.mv.

  • If header.md is present, its value MUST be the DNS domain name about which a VBR query was made.
  • If header.mv is present, its value MUST be the DNS domain name that was queried as the potential voucher for the header.md domain.

When the query was based on a VBR-Info header field in the incoming message, header.md is typically taken from its md tag and header.mv is typically one of the values of its mv tag. RFC 5518 allows other ways to choose the subject domain or vouchers, and a server could even run a VBR query when no VBR-Info field is present, based on local policy. In any of these cases the verifying server MAY generate an Authentication-Results field to relay the result.
sections.eli5: The note has two blanks: which sender's name was checked, and which trusted friend was asked. Fill in the two names and you are done.

sections.title: VBR Result Codes
sections.content:
The memo also adds the method vbr to five existing result names in the "Email Authentication Result Names" registry:

  • none: no valid VBR-Info header was found in the message, or a domain name to query could not be determined.
  • pass: a VBR query was completed and the vouching service gave a positive response.
  • fail: a VBR query was completed and the service did not give a positive response, or the message contained multiple VBR-Info header fields with different mc values.
  • temperror: the query could not be completed because of an error that is likely transient, such as a temporary DNS error. A later attempt may produce a final result.
  • permerror: the query could not be completed because of an error that is likely not transient, such as a permanent DNS error. A later attempt is unlikely to produce a final result.
sections.eli5: The note can say "no answer needed," "the friend said yes," "the friend said no," "the phone line was busy, try again," or "the number is broken."

sections.title: An Example Header
sections.content:
The appendix shows a message signed with DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) that also carried a VBR-Info header field. On receipt, the md= value in VBR-Info matched the d= value in the DKIM signature, and the signature verified, so a VBR query was performed.

The vouching service, voucher.example.org, indicated that the sender can be trusted, so a pass result was included in the Authentication-Results field added before delivery. It reads vbr=pass with header.md=newyork.example.com and header.mv=voucher.example.org.
sections.eli5: A message is checked two ways, and the trusted friend says yes, so the mailroom writes "pass" next to both checks.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo creates a mechanism for relaying VBR results using the structure already defined by RFC 5451. It adds no security analysis of its own and points readers to the Security Considerations sections of RFC 5451 and RFC 5518.
sections.eli5: This memo only adds a new kind of note. For safety advice, read the rules for the notes themselves and for the vouching system.

items.label: No query
items.desc: No valid VBR-Info header, or no domain to query.

items.label: Vouched
items.desc: Query completed with a positive response.

items.label: Not vouched
items.desc: Query completed without a positive response, or conflicting mc values.

items.label: Transient error
items.desc: Query could not complete; a later attempt may succeed.

items.label: Permanent error
items.desc: Query could not complete; a later attempt is unlikely to succeed.
